newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed sharply higher on fund buying and speculative short-covering. Volume was an impressive 16,733 lots, the highest level in many months, with buyers rushing in as London chased the sharp New York advance on Tuesday after predictions of a low Brazilian crop in 1997/98. However, some traders in London were puzzled by the reaction to the news that Brazil's 1997/98 crop could hover around 19 million bags as this unofficial estimate by the government followed earlier producer estimates of an even lower crop of 17 million bags. January added $96 to close at $1,338 per tonne while March increased by $76 to close at $1,303 per tonne. In New York arabica futures were not able to extend yesterday's sharp rise inspired by improving technical signals and increased speculation that the Brazilian 1997/98 harvest will be small. More rain is anticipated for southern Brazil in the next week which will not help crop prospects. March and May lost 45 points to close at 118.90 cents/lb and 116.60 cents/lb respectively. The outer months lost between 15 and 145 points.

VIETNAM - Vietnam's robusta coffee crop is coming in at full speed on the back of dry weather in the main producing province of Dak Lak and total exports could reach 4.2 million 60-kg bags, industry sources said. The coffee season in Vietnam usually runs from November to late February. Rains pounded Dak Lak last year, hindering the drying of the beans and raising concerns over mould. Those worries now appear to be on hold. Dak Lak produces about two thirds of Vietnam's coffee exports.

JAPAN - Japan imported 449,429 bags in November 1996, 29 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 5.215 million bags, 3.7 per cent more than was imported in the year-ago period. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply by 12 per cent to 5.324 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/November 1996 were Brazil (0.986 vs 1.096 million bags), Colombia (1.085 vs 0.903 million bags) and Indonesia (950,000 vs 753,100 bags).

BRAZIL - The Brazilian government sold 100 per cent of the 120,100 60-kg bags of coffee stocks offered in its auction on January 8, an official from the Banco do Brasil, which held the electronic auction, said. Prices ranged between 105.58 and 135.11 Reais ($102-130) a bag, with the weighted average price 112.79 Reais ($108.45) a bag, the official said. Roasters pointed out that the complete sell out is a clear sign that the government needs to raise the size of its sales. David Nahum, secretary general of the Brazilian Coffee Industry Association (ABIC) said that the next auction should be a minimum of 200,000 bags. Monthly Brazilian auctions for the 1996/97 coffee year (July/June) currently have a limit of 200,000 bags. The sale on January 8 was in fact the largest so far reflecting the decreasing availability of coffee from the 1996/97 harvest.
